sentences.en: Reporter Andrew Anderson is from the UK, but today he lives in Sofia, the capital city of Bulgaria.
sentences.zh: 记者安德鲁·安德森来自英国，但如今他住在保加利亚首都索非亚。

sentences.en: Andrew moved to Bulgaria because that's where his wife Victoria grew up.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁搬到保加利亚是因为他的妻子维多利亚在那里长大。

sentences.en: I came for a summer to try it out, and I just fell in love with it.
sentences.zh: 我来这里住了一个夏天想体验一下，然后就彻底爱上了这里。

sentences.en: The city was charmingly chaotic with a thriving art scene.
sentences.zh: 这座城市迷人地充满混乱，同时有着蓬勃发展的艺术氛围。

sentences.en: They stayed through one summer, then a second.
sentences.zh: 他们在那里度过了一个夏天，然后是第二个夏天。

sentences.en: And after two years in Sofia, Andrew and Victoria put down roots.
sentences.zh: 在索非亚生活两年后，安德鲁和维多利亚扎下了根。

sentences.en: They decided to save money by moving out of their centrally located rental
sentences.zh: 他们决定搬出位于市中心的出租屋来省点钱，

sentences.en: and into a little apartment owned by Victoria's family.
sentences.zh: 搬进了一间由维多利亚家人拥有的的小公寓里。

sentences.en: I was kind of a bit worried about it because Vicky had told me that
sentences.zh: 我当时其实有点担心，因为薇姬曾经告诉我，

sentences.en: it's really small and really crappy and really dingy,
sentences.zh: 这房子真的很小、很破、又很暗淡，

sentences.en: and I shouldn't have any expectations that I'm going to enjoy it,
sentences.zh: 而且我不应该对能喜欢这里抱有任何期待，

sentences.en: and maybe we won't even move there because maybe it's going to be too much for me
sentences.zh: 也许我们甚至都不会搬过去，因为这对我来说可能压力太大了，

sentences.en: and I won't be able to cope with it.
The apartment was in an old communist-built neighborhood called Slavia
sentences.zh: 这间公寓位于一个名为斯拉维亚的共产主义时期建造的老旧社区，
属于一个叫克拉斯诺切洛的地区。

sentences.en: Which literally translates as beautiful village.
sentences.zh: 它的字面意思就是美丽的村庄。

sentences.en: I can confirm it is not a beautiful village anymore.
sentences.zh: 我可以证实，这里现在已经算不上什么美丽的村庄了。

sentences.en: Now it's kind of maybe what you would have in mind if you were thinking of stereotypical
sentences.zh: 现在的它大概符合你对那种刻板印象中的

sentences.en: Lots of tower blocks, lots of kiosks and things like that around.
sentences.zh: 周围有很多高层住宅楼、很多小卖部之类的地方。

sentences.en: The first time Andrew went to see the apartment, he had trouble even finding it.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁第一次去看这套公寓时，甚至费了一番功夫才找到它。

sentences.en: To get there, he had to walk through a maze of overgrown paths and unmarked buildings.
sentences.zh: 为了到达那里，他不得不穿过一片杂草丛生的羊肠小道和没有门牌号的建筑迷宫。

sentences.en: When he finally managed to find the right building, he still had to climb seven flights of stairs.
sentences.zh: 当他终于找到对的楼时，还得爬七层楼梯。

sentences.en: But inside his new apartment, it was all worth it.
sentences.zh: 但一进到他的新公寓里，这一切就都值了。

sentences.en: When I got to the apartment and looked out the window, I was like, what a beautiful view.
sentences.zh: 当我走进公寓往窗外望去时，我想，这景色多美啊。

sentences.en: And once you're looking down on the neighborhood, suddenly it looks totally different
sentences.zh: 一旦你俯瞰这个社区，它突然间看起来就完全不同了，

sentences.en: because from the ground level, it's very disorganized, cluttered, messy.
sentences.zh: 因为从地面水平来看，这里非常杂乱无章、拥挤且凌乱。

sentences.en: But once you get up here, all you can really see is trees with little apartment blocks poking up
sentences.zh: 但一旦你来到这里，你真正能看到的只有绿树，夹杂着一座座小型公寓楼

sentences.en: So it's a totally different perspective.
sentences.zh: 所以这完全是一个不同的视角。

sentences.en: Seen from above, Sofia looks less like a city and more like a foreSt.
sentences.zh: 从高处俯瞰，索非亚看起来与其说是一座城市，不如说是一片森林。

sentences.en: And what at first looked to Andrew like a mess of winding footpaths and untamed greenery
sentences.zh: 起初在安德鲁看来是一团乱麻的蜿蜒小路和野蛮生长的绿植，

sentences.en: turned out to be one of Sofia's most iconic features.
sentences.zh: 结果却成了索非亚最具标志性的特征之一。

sentences.en: There's a few different things that people call them.
sentences.zh: 人们对它们有几种不同的称呼。

sentences.en: And the main term is like Meždublokové, which just means literally between the blocks.
sentences.zh: 主要的术语是Meždublokové，字面意思就是楼栋之间。

sentences.en: These green spaces between apartment buildings in Sofia are also known as interblock parks.
sentences.zh: 索非亚这些公寓楼之间的绿地也被称为“楼间公园”。

sentences.en: They're not even fully documented, so you don't really know how many there are.
sentences.zh: 它们甚至没有被完全记录在案，所以你根本不知道到底有多少个。

sentences.en: The spaces aren't really parks in the Western sense.
sentences.zh: 这些空间并不是西方意义上的那种公园。

sentences.en: And since they all flow together, it's hard to tell where one ends and another begins.
sentences.zh: 而且由于它们全都融为一体，你很难分清哪里是一个公园的终点，哪里又是另一个的起点。

sentences.en: The general effect is a series of walkable rivers of green space running through the city.
sentences.zh: 整体呈现出的效果就像是一条条贯穿城市的绿化步行河。

sentences.en: I could walk through old communist blocks without ever going on a road,
sentences.zh: 我可以穿过老旧的共产主义居民楼而不用走任何马路，

sentences.en: just through these parks, because there's a footpath and then you get to a small park.
sentences.zh: 只需穿过这些公园，因为这里有一条小路，然后你会来到一个小公园，

sentences.en: And then a footpath, maybe a bigger park, maybe just a really little one with only one swing.
sentences.zh: 接着又是一条小路，也许是一个更大的公园，也许只是一个只有一个秋千的极小公园。

sentences.en: Maybe one that's bigger and has like 10 pieces of furniture in it.
sentences.zh: 也许有的比较大，里面有大约10件休闲设施。

sentences.en: You know, with everyone with their clothes like strung all the way across the thing,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，每个人都把衣服晾在横跨各处的晾衣绳上，

sentences.en: sort of looks like an early Scorsese film or something like that.
sentences.zh: 看起来有点像早期的马丁·斯科塞斯电影或者诸如此类的东西。

sentences.en: The park closest to Andrew's house is pretty typical of the form,
sentences.zh: 离安德鲁家最近的公园非常符合这种形式的特点，

sentences.en: if a bit more on the rustic side.
I would guess half a football field in this case.
sentences.zh: 我猜这里大概相当于半个足球场大小。

sentences.en: There's a big globe climbing frame.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个大型的地球仪攀爬架。

sentences.en: There's two ping pong tables, both of which don't have nets anymore.
sentences.zh: 这里有两张乒乓球桌，但两张桌子都已经没有球网了。

sentences.en: But they're perfect for like improvised picnic tables.
sentences.zh: 但它们非常适合当作临时的野餐桌。

sentences.en: So people just put their beers on them.
sentences.zh: 所以人们就把啤酒直接放在上面。

sentences.en: Soon after Andrew and his family moved into the little apartment in Slavia,
sentences.zh: 安德鲁和家人搬进斯拉维亚的小公寓后不久，

sentences.en: they found themselves using the Interblock Park as a combination playground, event space, and social club.
sentences.zh: 他们发现自己经常把这个楼间公园当成游乐场、活动场地和社交俱乐部的结合体来使用。

sentences.en: You end up making friends quite quickly.
sentences.zh: 你很快就能结交到朋友。

sentences.en: I lived in Manchester for eight years and I didn't know a single one of my neighbors.
sentences.zh: 我在曼彻斯特住了八年，却连一个邻居都不认识。

sentences.en: And I know quite a lot of the people in this block and even more in the surrounding neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 而我认识这栋楼里的很多人，甚至还认识周边社区的更多人。

sentences.en: Andrew is the only foreigner in his apartment block.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁是他这栋公寓楼里唯一的外国人。

sentences.en: He started going to the park every day, meeting neighbors who had grown up in Slavia
sentences.zh: 他开始每天去公园，结识那些在斯拉维亚长大、

sentences.en: and who saw the parks mostly as just another part of their daily landscape.
sentences.zh: 把这些公园仅仅视为日常生活景观一部分的邻居们。

sentences.en: Then Andrew met someone else as fascinated by the Interblock parks as he was.
sentences.zh: 后来，安德鲁遇到了另一个人，她和安德鲁一样对楼间公园充满着迷。

sentences.en: My name is Ashira Morris and I am a freelance reporter based between Sofia and Florida.
sentences.zh: 我叫阿希拉·莫里斯，是一名常驻索非亚和佛罗里达的自由记者。

sentences.en: Andrew and Ashira are both foreigners married to Bulgarians.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁和阿希拉都是娶了或嫁给保加利亚人的外国人。

sentences.en: And they shared a certain outsider's awe about the parks.
sentences.zh: 他们对这些公园有着某种身为局外人的惊叹之情。

sentences.en: I think for both of us, these are spaces that like, especially as people coming in from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我想对我们俩来说，这些空间就像是，特别是作为从美国
会觉得它们真的非常特别。

sentences.en: And I feel like it's one of my favorite things about the city in a way.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在某种程度上，这也是我最喜欢这座城市的特点之一。

sentences.en: Sofia's Interblock parks were both unexpected and charming,
sentences.zh: 索非亚的楼间公园既出人意料又迷人，

sentences.en: especially coming from the tidy streets of Manchester or the suburban sprawl of northern Florida.
sentences.zh: 特别是对于来自曼彻斯特整洁街道或是佛罗里达北部城郊无序扩张的人来说更是如此。

sentences.en: So they both took notice after a rumor started spreading through Andrew's neighborhood
sentences.zh: 因此，当安德鲁的社区开始流传起当地公园可能要被推平的传闻时，他们两人都注意到了这件事。

sentences.en: that his local park might be bulldozed.
sentences.zh: 当时，当我第一次听到这个消息时，我想，这怎么可能？

sentences.en: At the time, when I first heard about it, I was like, well, how's that possible?
sentences.zh: 这些楼栋之间根本没有多大空间。

sentences.en: There's not even really much space between these blocks.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，大概就两个网球场那么大。

sentences.en: Like I said, it's like two tennis courts.
sentences.zh: 而且我一直理所当然地认为这是一片公共公园绿地。

sentences.en: And also I was working under the assumption that this was public park space.
sentences.zh: 所以为什么要在这上面搞建设呢？

sentences.en: So why would you build on it?
sentences.zh: 不久后，一张规划公示贴了出来。

sentences.en: Soon, a planning notice showed up.
sentences.zh: 市政府已经批准了一家开发商建造两栋新公寓楼的申请。

sentences.en: The city had given permission to a developer to put up two new apartment buildings.
sentences.zh: 它们将建在楼间公园的旁边。

sentences.en: They would go up next to the Interblock park.
sentences.zh: 但开发商需要一条通往大楼地下停车场的出入道路。

sentences.en: But the developers needed an access road into the building's parking garage.
sentences.zh: 他们计划把路修在现在那些野餐桌的正下方。

sentences.en: They planned to build it exactly where the picnic tables are now.
sentences.zh: 我感到非常震惊，因为在英国，要想做到这一点要困难得多，

sentences.en: I was shocked because in England, it would be much harder to do that
sentences.zh: 因为那里往往有非常严格的规划法律。

sentences.en: because there tends to be such rigid planning laws.
sentences.zh: 而且我必须说，我是在一个叫贝克韦尔的国家公园里长大的，

sentences.en: And I have to say, I grew up living inside a national park in a place called Bakewell
sentences.zh: 那个地方位于峰区国家公园内。

sentences.en: that's in the Peak District National Park.
sentences.zh: 所以在那里搞规划，比如任何规划许可，

sentences.en: So getting stuff planned, like any planning permission there,
sentences.zh: 哪怕只是在花园里放一个花园小矮人雕像，有时都可能会相当棘手。

sentences.en: even to put a garden gnome in your garden can be quite tricky sometimes.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁和阿希拉开始与专家交谈，

sentences.en: Andrew and Ashura started talking to experts,
sentences.zh: 试图理解索非亚城市景观中如此标志性的一部分

sentences.en: trying to understand how an iconic part of Sofia's urban landscape
sentences.zh: 怎么会如此轻易地消失。
他们很快发现，自从20世纪80年代末保加利亚共产主义政权倒台以来，

sentences.en: What they quickly discovered is that since the fall of Bulgarian communism
sentences.zh: 索非亚已经失去了超过一半的绿地。

sentences.en: in the late 1980s, Sofia has lost more than half of its green space.
sentences.zh: 为了解这是如何发生的以及剩余公园的命运将会如何，

sentences.en: To understand how it happened and what the fate of the remaining parks might be,
sentences.zh: 他们不得不追溯到这座首都城市本身的起源。

sentences.en: they had to go back to the origin of the capital city itself.
sentences.zh: 索非亚是一座非常年轻的首都。

sentences.en: Sofia is a really young capital.
sentences.zh: 所以你面对的是一个曾经是城市、但并不是大城市的地方。

sentences.en: So you have a place that has been a city, but not a big city.
sentences.zh: 在成为一座由公园和公寓组成的城市之前，索非亚曾是个沉睡的地方。

sentences.en: Before it became a city of parks and apartments, Sofia was a sleepy place.
sentences.zh: 它在二战期间遭到过轰炸，但没有其他欧洲首都那么严重，

sentences.en: It was bombed during World War II, but not as badly as other European capitals,
sentences.zh: 部分原因在于当时这座城市的规模没那么大，没什么可炸的。

sentences.en: partly because there just wasn't as much of a city to bomb.
sentences.zh: 就整个国家而言，在共产主义时期之前，保加利亚一直是个非常依重农业的国家。

sentences.en: Bulgaria as a country overall, until communism, was very agrarian.

sentences.zh: 当时并没有那种在工厂工作、

sentences.en: There was not a proletariat that was working in the factories
sentences.zh: 进行组织并起义的无产阶级。

sentences.en: and like organizing and rising up.
sentences.zh: 这里绝大多数都是农民。
保加利亚共产党于1946年上台执政，

sentences.en: The Bulgarian Communist Party came to power in 1946,
sentences.zh: 当时这座城市仅有40万人口，周围环绕着农田。

sentences.en: when the city was home to just 400,000 people and was surrounded by farmland.
sentences.zh: 保加利亚新共产党政府的目标

sentences.en: The goal of Bulgaria's new communist government
sentences.zh: 是将索非亚转变为一个现代化的工业首都。

sentences.en: was to transform Sofia into a modern industrial capital.
sentences.zh: 他们看着这些农田，觉得这是一张白纸。

sentences.en: And they're looking to this farmland and they're seeing this is kind of a blank slate.
sentences.zh: 正当保加利亚的城市规划者们构想一个新的索非亚时，

sentences.en: As Bulgarian city planners were dreaming up a new Sofia,
sentences.zh: 他们明确知道自己对郊区毫无兴趣。

sentences.en: they knew what they were not interested in, suburbs.
sentences.zh: 保加利亚的城市规划教科书将当时在美国涌现的那种单户住宅

sentences.en: Bulgarian urban planning textbooks called the kind of single family homes
popping up in America at the time,
sentences.zh: 取而代之的是，他们选择了通过苏联引入的法国现代主义。
保加利亚从来都不是苏联的一部分。

sentences.en: Instead, they opted for French modernism via the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 它有自己的共产主义独裁者和自治权，

sentences.en: Bulgaria was never a part of the USSR.
sentences.zh: 但同时也非常忠诚，在许多不同方面都与苏联的做法高度保持一致。

sentences.en: It had its own communist dictator and its own self-governance,
sentences.zh: 这其中也包括他们的城市规划。

sentences.en: but was also very loyal and very much in step with what the USSR was doing on a lot of different fronts.
sentences.zh: 这位是建筑历史学家兼评论家阿内塔·瓦西列娃。

sentences.en: And that includes with their city planning.
sentences.zh: 有一位建筑历史学家兼理论家斯坦尼斯瓦夫·福莫斯，

sentences.en: Here's architectural historian and critic Aneta Vasileva.
sentences.zh: 他曾说过，如果你必须用三个词来形容战后时期，

sentences.en: There is one architectural historian and theorist, Stanislav Formos,
sentences.zh: 这三个词就是：废墟、斯大林和勒·柯布西耶。

sentences.en: who is saying that if you have to describe the post-war period in three words,
sentences.zh: 斯大林、废墟和勒·柯布西耶这三个名字也恰好出现在我们在9IPI开的每一个选题策划会上。

sentences.en: these words would have been ruins, Stalin and Le Corbusier.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，这位瑞士裔法国建筑师勒·柯布西耶的作品启发了苏联，

sentences.en: Stalin, ruins and Le Corbusier also happen to be in every story pitch meeting we have at 9IPI.
sentences.zh: 使其在城市规划中走向开放式几何布局。

sentences.en: Anyway, the work of Swiss-French architect Le Corbusier inspired the USSR
sentences.zh: 这种为人民服务的建筑、为社会服务的建筑，

sentences.en: to move toward open geometry in its urban planning.
sentences.zh: 在广阔绿地中采用独立建筑结构来发展城市的模范方式，

sentences.en: This kind of architecture for the people, architecture for society,
sentences.zh: 以及将住房、生活、休闲和工作功能进行区分的理念，

sentences.en: model way of developing cities of freestanding structures within vast green areas
sentences.zh: 都是为了重建战争造成的满目疮痍。

sentences.en: and separate functions of housing, living, recreation and work
sentences.zh: 据我所知，勒·柯布西耶本人曾与莫斯科的一些主要城市规划者有过书信往来。

sentences.en: to rebuild the devastations of war.
sentences.zh: 还有一个轶事说，索非亚所有的城市规划者都在办公室里挂着勒·柯布西耶的肖像，

sentences.en: Le Corbusier himself, I believe, has a correspondence with some of the main city planners in Moscow.
sentences.zh: 就像你们挂列宁肖像那样。

sentences.en: And there is an anecdote that like all of the city planners in Sofia had a portrait
sentences.zh: 但除了勒·柯布西耶简洁、鲜明的现代主义之外，

sentences.en: of Le Corbusier in their offices in the way that you would have the Lenin portrait.
sentences.zh: 苏联城市规划者也对英国的田园城市运动产生了浓厚兴趣。

sentences.en: But alongside Le Corbusier's clean, sharp modernism,
sentences.zh: 这个理念是，城市规划者可以将乡村引入城市，

sentences.en: Soviet urban planners were also drawn to the British Garden City movement.
sentences.zh: 融入零星的自然景观来抵消噪音和污染。

sentences.en: The idea was that urban planners could bring the country into the city,
sentences.zh: 苏联城市规划者接受了田园城市理念并将其本土化。

sentences.en: incorporating pockets of nature to counterbalance noise and pollution.
sentences.zh: 他们谈论诸如让绿色空气走廊穿过城市之类的概念。

sentences.en: Soviet city planners embraced the Garden City and made it their own.
sentences.zh: 我发现这种表达方式真的很美，人们把这些环境元素

sentences.en: They talk about like having corridors of green air like move through the city.
sentences.zh: 谈论得好像它们被赋予了某种实体生命一般。

sentences.en: And I find it really beautiful just the way that people talk about these environmental elements
sentences.zh: 我发现这种人们将环境元素视为某种拟人化存在的谈论方式真的非常美妙。

sentences.en: The dream of a fully actualized Garden City quickly spread across the Eastern Bloc.
sentences.zh: 完全实现的“花园城市”梦想迅速传遍了东欧集团。

sentences.en: The model seemed perfectly suited to communist ideals.
sentences.zh: 这种模式似乎非常契合共产主义的理想。

sentences.en: It was very important for them to have massive public spaces
sentences.zh: 对他们而言，拥有大规模的公共空间非常重要，

sentences.en: because the regime was supposed to elevate the public realm.
sentences.zh: 因为该政权本应提升公众领域。

sentences.en: And what better way to elevate the public realm
sentences.zh: 还有什么比提升公众领域更好的方式呢？

sentences.en: but by having really magnificent public spaces, including parks.
sentences.zh: 那就是拥有真正宏伟的公共空间，包括公园。

sentences.en: Sonia Hurt is a professor of landscape architecture
sentences.zh: 索尼亚·赫特是一位景观建筑学教授，

sentences.en: who first experienced landscape and architecture growing up in Sofia.
sentences.zh: 她在索菲亚长大，最早在那里体验到了景观与建筑。

sentences.en: She says that communist countries were far from the only places
sentences.zh: 她表示，共产主义国家绝不是唯一试图

sentences.en: looking to put these ideals into action.
sentences.zh: 将这些理想付诸实践的地方。

sentences.en: I think it's easy to assume that, you know,
sentences.zh: 我认为人们很容易觉得，你知道的，

sentences.en: communism and capitalism were different in terms of urban design,
sentences.zh: 共产主义和资本主义在城市设计方面有所不同，

sentences.en: but I actually don't think they were.
sentences.zh: 但我其实认为它们并无二致。

sentences.en: In terms of the design features and the design ideology of the parks,
sentences.zh: 就公园的设计特征和设计意识形态而言，

sentences.en: I don't think that's any different.
It's simply that they were more important to the socialist regime
sentences.zh: 只是对社会主义政权而言，它们比在资本主义国家中

sentences.en: than they were in capitalist countries.
And also they had a greater opportunity.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也拥有更大的机遇。

sentences.en: Capitalists and communists might have had similar tastes in city planning,
sentences.zh: 资本主义者和共产主义者在城市规划上的品味或许相似，

sentences.en: but they had very different approaches to implement that planning.
sentences.zh: 但他们在落实这些规划时采取了截然不同的方法。

sentences.en: Starting in 1948, the Bulgarian government nationalized all private property.
sentences.zh: 从1948年开始，保加利亚政府将所有私有财产收归国有。

sentences.en: That meant that if you owned any land in or around Sofia,
sentences.zh: 这意味着如果你在索菲亚市内或周边拥有任何土地，

sentences.en: it became the property of the state.
The most you might get in return was an apartment or two
sentences.zh: 你能拿到的最多回报，也就是你前住所附近

sentences.en: in a block near your former home.
I think it's just very utilitarian, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常实用主义，不是吗？

sentences.en: Like you need somewhere, like the minimum thing you need to live is an apartment.
sentences.zh: 就像你需要某个地方，生存的最低需求就是一套公寓。

sentences.en: So you get an apartment, but the farmer's living in the farmhouse.
sentences.zh: 所以你得到了一套公寓，但农民住在农舍里。

sentences.en: He'll get an apartment in exchange for his farmhouse,
sentences.zh: 他会用农舍换来一套公寓，

sentences.en: but not for the land, because that's now going to become a factory.
sentences.zh: 但换不来土地，因为那现在要变成一座工厂。

sentences.en: That's now going to become more apartment blocks.
sentences.zh: 那现在要变成更多的公寓楼。

sentences.en: That's now going to become a collectivized farm.
sentences.zh: 那现在要变成一个集体农庄。

sentences.en: Nationalization took many people away from the land
sentences.zh: 国有化让许多人离开了

sentences.en: their families had worked for generations,
sentences.zh: 他们家族世世代代耕作的土地，

sentences.en: but it also cleared the way for Bulgaria to put the inspiration
sentences.zh: 但也为保加利亚将现代花园城市的灵感

sentences.en: for a modern garden city into action.
And because they don't have to go plot by plot by plot,
sentences.zh: 而且由于他们不必一块地挨着一块地、

sentences.en: neighbor by neighbor by neighbor, and like get permission,
sentences.zh: 一家邻居挨着一家邻居地去逐一争取许可，

sentences.en: they are really able to do that on a scale that is bigger and more all-encompassing
sentences.zh: 他们确实能够以一种在资本主义社会中无法实现的、

sentences.en: than it was able to happen in a capitalist society.
sentences.zh: 更大且更包容的规模来做到这一点。

sentences.en: In the decades following the seizure of private land,
sentences.zh: 在夺取私有土地后的几十年里，

sentences.en: Bulgarian city planners fundamentally transformed the landscape of Sofia,
sentences.zh: 保加利亚的城市规划者从根本上改变了索菲亚的地貌，

sentences.en: a series of communist-planned neighborhoods fanned outwards from the city center.
sentences.zh: 一系列共产主义规划的社区从市中心向外扇形展开。

sentences.en: The earliest of these neighborhoods all tend to have a certain distinctive setup.
sentences.zh: 这些最早的社区往往都有着某种独特的布局。

sentences.en: If you think about college campuses that are very much a campus,
sentences.zh: 如果你回想一下那种真正的大学校园，

sentences.en: where you've got residential blocks for students that were built in the 50s and 60s,
sentences.zh: 里面有50和60年代建造的学生住宅楼，

sentences.en: but they're sat in a park in a way that's landscaped,
sentences.zh: 但它们坐落在一个经过景观美化的公园里，

sentences.en: and then it all drains into the center where there's the bigger buildings like the big library,
sentences.zh: 然后所有的排水都汇聚到中心，那里有更大的建筑，比如大图书馆，

sentences.en: you know, the student union, things like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，学生会大楼之类的。

sentences.en: It kind of has a similar feel to that.
sentences.zh: 它带有一种与之相似的感觉。

sentences.en: Sofia city planners were intentional about seemingly everything.
sentences.zh: 索菲亚的城市规划者对看似一切的事物都经过了精心设计。

sentences.en: They built apartment blocks in a specific orientation that would trap heat from the sun in winter
sentences.zh: 他们以特定的朝向建造公寓楼，以便在冬天吸收太阳热量，

sentences.en: without getting too hot in the summer.
sentences.zh: 同时又不会在夏天变得太热。

sentences.en: The buildings were also placed so that they would block the noise from surrounding highways.
sentences.zh: 建筑的摆放位置也能阻挡来自周围高速公路的噪音。

sentences.en: And on top of the housing,
the new neighborhoods had all the basic amenities that you might need as a resident.
sentences.zh: 这些新社区还具备了居民所需的所有基本设施。

sentences.en: There were hospitals, community centers, and schools.
sentences.zh: 这里有医院、社区中心和学校。

sentences.en: So you have a kindergarten every 200 meters,
sentences.zh: 所以每隔200米就有一所幼儿园，

sentences.en: and the upper grade schools every 500 meters,
sentences.zh: 每隔500米就有一所高年级学校，

sentences.en: because, you know, a smaller child can't walk as far.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，小孩子走不了那么远。

sentences.en: It must have been an absolute wet dream for someone like an egotist like Le Corbusier.
sentences.zh: 对于勒·柯布西耶这样的自大狂来说，这绝对是春梦一般的美事。

sentences.en: And no wonder he was like going to visit Moscow.
sentences.zh: 难怪他会去访问莫斯科。

sentences.en: Surrounding all of this new infrastructure were Sofia's inner block parks.
sentences.zh: 环绕着所有这些新基础设施的是索菲亚的街坊内部公园。

sentences.en: They were seen as an important way to put the government's communist ideals into action.
sentences.zh: 它们被视为将政府的共产主义理想付诸实践的重要途径。

sentences.en: The urban planners under communism were really specifically concerned
sentences.zh: 共产主义时期的城市规划者特别关心的，

sentences.en: about everyone having an equal share of everything.
sentences.zh: 是让每个人都能平等待享有一切。

sentences.en: And that includes trying to think of nature as something that you can equally parse.
sentences.zh: 其中也包括将自然视为可以平等分割之物的理念。

sentences.en: So they wanted to make it so that everyone would have a certain amount of space in total.
sentences.zh: 因此他们希望确保每个人都能拥有一定总量的空间。

sentences.en: Most apartments built around this time were small,
sentences.zh: 这一时期建造的大多数公寓都很小，

sentences.en: because you weren't supposed to need that much private space.
sentences.zh: 因为你本就不需要那么多的私人空间。

sentences.en: the green spaces between are just an extension of your apartment.
sentences.zh: 中间的绿地就只是你公寓的延伸。

sentences.en: It's also part of what you're living in.
sentences.zh: 它也是你生活空间的一部分。

sentences.en: So anything that you maybe don't have in the house,
sentences.zh: 所以你在家里可能没有的东西，
你在外面或许都能拥有。

sentences.en: Okay, I don't have anywhere to sit.
And you definitely wouldn't have had a television.
sentences.zh: 而且你肯定不会有电视。

sentences.en: But there's loads of benches outside.
And there's people to hang out with.
sentences.zh: 还有可以一起闲逛的人。

sentences.en: Back then, with the nets still on them, probably.
sentences.zh: 在当时，上面可能还挂着网呢。

sentences.en: So that's what these spaces, at their best, can provide.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是这些空间在最佳状态下能够提供的东西。

sentences.en: And obviously, later, when they were let to fall to pieces,
sentences.zh: 很明显，后来当它们任由荒废时，

sentences.en: because you don't have anything else to fall back on.
sentences.zh: 因为你没有任何其他东西可以依靠。

sentences.en: Like, this should have been the thing that gives you the things you need to live.
sentences.zh: 就像，这本该是为你提供生活所需的事物。

sentences.en: And if you don't have those anymore,
then it's a bigger problem, actually, losing those spaces.
sentences.zh: 那么失去这些空间其实就是一个更大的问题。

sentences.en: Almost as soon as the communist government began transforming Sofia,
sentences.zh: 几乎在共产主义政府开始改造索菲亚的同时，

sentences.en: it was running up against the limits of its own ambition.
sentences.zh: 它就遇到了自身雄心的极限。

sentences.en: The first communist-built neighborhoods had all the amenities,
sentences.zh: 第一批由共产主义建造的社区拥有一切设施，

sentences.en: but the government couldn't afford to keep them up.
sentences.zh: 但政府无力维持它们的运转。

sentences.en: Under communism, there is a certain level of maintenance
sentences.zh: 在共产主义制度下，城市最初会提供

sentences.en: that comes from the city in the beginning.
But there is also what's called Leninski Saputnitsi,
sentences.zh: 但也有所谓的“列宁共青团星期六”或列宁义务劳动，

sentences.en: which is this, quote-unquote, volunteer work,
where the idea was that, like, the people in the blocks
sentences.zh: 其理念是，居住在这些楼里的居民

sentences.en: would go and kind of do the work of maintaining
and cleaning up the spaces around them

sentences.zh: 就在这些街区内部公园里。

sentences.en: I would say this is volunteering with big air quotes.
sentences.zh: 我要说，这是打着极大引号的志愿服务。

sentences.en: But as the decades go on,
the maintenance just starts to fall off.
sentences.zh: 维护工作开始逐渐荒废。
甚至根本没有建设完工。
游乐设施，甚至连长椅都没有。

sentences.en: I remember the green spaces between the housing blocks.
sentences.zh: 我记得住宅楼之间的绿地。

sentences.en: They were not very well maintained, to be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 说实话，它们维护得并不是很好。

sentences.en: During socialism, I think that we were simply running out of money.
sentences.zh: 在社会主义时期，我认为我们实在是资金短缺。

sentences.en: So the state would invest in the most ceremonial places,
sentences.zh: 因此，国家会将资金投入到那些最讲究门面的地方，

sentences.en: the Bulgarian Communist Party reached the end of its long decline.
sentences.zh: 保加利亚共产党走到了其漫长衰落的终点。

sentences.en: In November, the dictator Todor Zhivkov was forced out of office.
sentences.zh: 11月，独裁者托多尔·日夫科夫被迫下台。

sentences.en: And by December, his replacement was calling for free elections.
sentences.zh: 到了12月，他的继任者开始呼吁举行自由选举。
保加利亚的共产主义倒台了。

sentences.en: the inter-block parks were the last thing on anyone's mind.
sentences.zh: 街区间公园成了所有人最不会去想的事情。

sentences.en: The 90s, it was a total collapse.
I mean, honestly, it looked like a war had come.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，老实说，看起来就像刚打过仗一样。

sentences.en: I mean, the least thing the municipality would wonder about was neighbors.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，市政部门最不操心的就是邻里社区了。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那简直就像是，哈！

sentences.en: You just go there, it looks like, you know,
sentences.zh: 你只要去到那里，看起来就像是，你知道的，

sentences.en: I mean, no one's cutting the grass.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，没有人修剪草坪。

sentences.en: Bulgaria's transition to democracy was peaceful,
sentences.zh: 保加利亚向民主的过渡是和平的，

sentences.en: but that doesn't mean it was smooth.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着它一帆风顺。

sentences.en: In the immediate aftermath of the collapse,
sentences.zh: 在崩溃发生后的直接余波中，

sentences.en: there was a lot of optimism about democracy and capitalism.
sentences.zh: 人们对民主和资本主义充满了乐观情绪。

sentences.en: But now, the new democratic government decided to undertake
sentences.zh: 但现在，新的民主政府决定着手承担

sentences.zh: 一项荒谬复杂的工作，即甄别

sentences.zh: 在共产主义政权下被没收的土地，

这被称为武伊尼科夫法案，

sentences.en: and this was part of the policies in the 90s
sentences.zh: 这也是90年代政策的一部分

sentences.en: to compensate people from this long-term socialist nationalization
sentences.zh: 旨在对长期社会主义国有化造成的人们进行补偿

sentences.zh: 很快就变成了一场灾难的绝对噩梦般的盛宴。

sentences.zh: 请记住，索非亚市的大部分地区

sentences.zh: 是建立在40年代开始被国有化的土地上的

sentences.en: and almost none of it was recognizable anymore as farmland.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有多少还能被认出是农田。

sentences.en: The government solution took that into account.
sentences.zh: 政府的解决方案考虑到了这一点。

sentences.en: Basically, if a building had been put on your family's land
sentences.zh: 基本上，如果在一块土地上建了建筑物

sentences.zh: 在过去的40年里，你可能会得到一些微不足道的补偿

The only way you could get land back
sentences.zh: 你唯一能拿回土地的方法

sentences.en: is if that land had been left undeveloped through all of communism.
sentences.zh: 就是这块土地在整个共产主义时期一直未被开发。

sentences.en: So it's very, I mean, well-intentioned.
sentences.zh: 所以这真的非常，我的意思是，是出于好意。

Back when communist planners set up their maps,
sentences.zh: 早在共产主义规划者绘制地图时

sentences.zh: 他们理所当然地认为他们永远不会开发公园绿地。

sentences.zh: 所以公园从未被正式列为受保护的绿地。

sentences.zh: 但现在，在这个充满私有财产的新世界里

sentences.en: which meant they could be given to private citizens
sentences.zh: 这意味着它们可以交还给普通公民

sentences.en: if you've been given land back as compensation,

为什么你不能卖掉它呢？

sentences.en: you get this land and you can do what you want with it.

sentences.zh: 并记得能够走在街区之间
